summary:
# NOTES: THE FATAL THREE (Mary Elizabeth Braddon), 3 vols

## Dramatis personae (key)
- **John Fausset**: stout, middle-aged, ex-wholesale silk merchant (Fausset & Co., St Paul's Churchyard; factory Lyons). Sold out of business, now MP-type ("the House"). Sole trustee of ward Fay's fortune.
- **Maud Fausset** (née Hon. Maud Donfrey, 3rd dau. of Lord Castle-Connell, Irish peer): ~28 in Vol I, tall, fair, fashionable, jealous, hysterical; married at 19; dies ~age 36 (heart disease) after ~2 yrs invalidism, soon after Mildred's 16th birthday.
- **Mildred Fausset** (later **Mildred Greswold**): golden hair, violet eyes. Age 7 in Vol I. Chaperoned by Miss Colville (governess). Pianist.
- **Fay** (Fanny Fausset, alias Vivien Faux): pale, thin, olive skin, huge black eyes, bad temper, gifted musician, improvises fairy tales. ~14 in Vol I.
- **Martha Bell**: Maud's former wet-nurse (Castle-Connell). ~48 in Vol I; iron-gray hair, no cap, black silk gown; Irish; hates Fay; "I" emphasis.
- **Meta**: Mildred's German maid. Maud's French maid unnamed.
- **Miss Constable**: proprietress of Streatham-area school where Fay was.
- **Gertrude Fausset**: John's only sister, Mildred's aunt. Milan student (Conservatoire), later Brighton spinster, 57 in Vol II; Lewes Crescent; St Edmund's church.
- **George Ransome / George Greswold**: 2nd son of Squire Ransome of Mapledown (Sussex Weald); mother (heiress) left him Enderby Manor (Hampshire, near Romsey) → assumed name Greswold. Oxford (Magdalen). Writer/scholar, ~30 when married; 13 years older than Mildred. Brother **Randolph** (married; daughters Rosalind—m. Sir Henry Mountford, Rainham Hall—and **Pamela Ransome**).
- **Lola (Laura) Greswold**: only child of George & Mildred; blue eyes, gold hair; dies age 12 of typhoid from polluted dairy well (Vol I).
- **Mrs Wadman**: dairy-woman, dismissed with husband; **Porter** (Dr Porter, village doctor); **Dr Hutchinson** (Southampton); **Mr Rollinson** (curate, Enderby; jovial, puns, poet; loves Lola; later writes to Mildred); **Mrs Mason** (carpenter's wife, lodgings); **Kassandra** (Irish setter); **Box** (Pamela's fox-terrier); **Puck** (Lola's dog).
- **Polly (Mary) Rainbow**: flaxen-haired village child, first typhoid death; widow mother Mrs Rainbow.
- **César Castellani** (also "Castleton" misnamed once): tall, slim, auburn/red-brown hair and pointed beard, reddish-brown eyes, milky pallor; "Judas" face; Milanese; Rugby & Cambridge; author of anonymous novel *Nepenthe*; tenor; pianist; father **Paolo Castellani** (composer; Milan; operas *La Donna del Pittore*, etc.); mother French, convent-educated at Roehampton. Lives on Gertrude's money, claims silk-trade grandfather link to Faussets.
- **Louise Hillersdon** (née Louise Lorraine): ex-courtesan, Irish gray eyes, now pious hostess at Riverdale (Tom Hillersdon, millionaire, Wiltshire squire).
- **Clement Cancellor**: Vicar of St Elizabeth's, Parchment Street; ascetic; Mildred's childhood tutor; anti-Deceased Wife's Sister Bill.
- **Mrs Tomkison (Cecilia)** & **Adam Tomkison**: Queen Anne's Gate; Cecilia = Mildred's friend, literary/æsthetic; Castellani lives in Queen Anne's Mansions.
- **Mr Maltravers**: Vicar of St Edmund's, Brighton (wants transept built).
- **Rev. Percival Cromer**: curate, son of Lord Lowestoft.
- **Lady Lochinvar** (widow, ex-O'Labacolly's daughter; Palais Montano, Nice); nephew **Malcolm Stuart** (~30, Scotch, freckled, ginger, blue eyes, ex-cavalry; heir; Pamela's fiancé).
- **Mr & Mrs Murray** (Scotch young matron; invalid husband).
- **Franz** (Swiss butler, Lewes Crescent); **Louisa** (Mildred's maid); **Albrecht** (courier); **Peterson** (Pamela's maid).
- **Mr Pergament** (Pergament & Pergament, Lincoln's Inn Fields).
- **Dr Leroy** (Nice asylum, St André); **Maria Castellani** (asylum singer, Paolo's cousin); Spanish nobleman inmate; "Blessed Virgin" woman.
- **Vivien Faux / Vivien Ransome**: George's 1st wife (= Fay). Died 24 April 1868, Nice area.
- **Delia Darcy** & sister: Irish belles, Nice.
- **Dresser/others**: Signora Vicenti (Florence hostess); Mr & Mrs Mortimer (artist & wife, Brussels/Florence); Mrs Holmby (Milan chaperon for Gertrude).

---

## VOLUME I — Book the First: CLOTHO; or Spinning the Thread

**Ch I "We have been so happy."** London, Upper Parchment Street (off Grosvenor Sq, Park Lane side). Maud and John discuss adopting Fay (13–14, orphan, John's ward, "distant relation", "kindred"). Maud: "golden circle of home-life." John: wants to fulfil duty; Fay will be "well married." Maud: "Had the mother no people?" Mildred (7) listening; pleads "Let the little girl come, mother." Maud submits. Mildred: will give Fay "second best doll" (wax-and-bran); not "best" (Paris walking-talking doll). John: "What a happy home it has been!"

**Ch II Fay.** Maud returns after 3 parties. John meets Fay at Streatham Common (school), brings her by hansom; trunk by four-wheeler. Fay: tall, thin, black frock, olive tint, "never much cared for." "I hate lessons." "I love books." Mildred: "I'll give you my very best doll." Fay embraces her. Bell's old room assigned to Fay (back, mews, chimney-pots, iron bed). Maud: Fay "so remarkably plain"; "owl in an ivy-bush." Morning-room (bow window, scarlet Japanese tea-table, bronze kettle with dragons, Virginian love-birds). Staircase: scarlet Japanese screen (down), blue-and-gold Algerian curtain (up). Maud's domain = 2nd floor; Mildred's bedroom (blue paper, brass bed) and schoolroom = 3rd floor.

**Ch III A Superior Person.** Mildred's need for love vs mother's social round. Maud jealous: "If one could only believe it were genuine." Fay's resentment of exclusion at afternoons. Bell's history: Martha Bell, lace-maker from Limerick; husband Patrick Bell, head gardener at Castle-Connell lodge by the Shannon; their first child died; Martha became wet-nurse for Maud; husband emigrated to Canada, died. Bell's power: "discovering the weak side of everybody's character." Bell vs Fay: Fay refuses Bell help; Bell's clothes shopping ("Oxford Street will do"). Miss Colville: "shockingly backward." Maud: "It is her disposition I am anxious about." Bell: "Ah, ma'am, and so am I."

**Ch IV All She Could Remember.** Season waning. Fay's shopping: mushroom hat, coarse brown straw ("hideous"). Bell interrogates Fay (on school, mother, father) — Fay refuses. Fay's childhood memories: cottage garden on windy chalk hill above sea; woman "Nounou"; fowls, cow, arrogant cock; tall column with statue; "Where do they go?" (ships). Taken by little gray-haired man on steamer; narrow bed; oval window; railway; patch of common with gorse. Then elderly prim lady (silk gown, gold watch) who taught English; ruddy-faced girl in lavender cotton. Then "great dark city" (London), classic portico school (shining laurels, rhododendrons, laburnums). Miss Constable's school: Fay's bad temper; quarrels; lost temper mid-class; rushed out; Miss Constable: "We will make a tabula rasa of a troublesome past... Miss Fausset must go." Fay's musical gifts: improvised fairy tales for Mildred (Beauty's father, Fatima's brothers, Bluebeard's castle). Bell: "I nursed your mamma." Fay's nights: schoolroom, sits till 9:30. Maud dislikes Fay; servants neglect her. The Hook (Chertsey–Windsor; long white house, double marble stair, Italian cupola, classic colonnade; river loop, willows). Mildred catches scarlet fever (called scarlatina) in August; Fay nurses; slept in truckle-bed in dressing-room. Maud: "Dear, sweet pet." Eavesdrop: Bell and Meta in sitting-room: Bell claims Fay is Mr Fausset's daughter ("Heiress, indeed! ...dropped from the moon"). Mildred resolves "sister" secret. Tea in tent: Mildred asks "why mayn't I call Fay sister?" Maud: "Bell is an impertinent person... my own old nurse." Fay: "I hate everybody else in this house." Maud: "wicked, ungrateful girl... I am very sorry I ever saw your face." Fausset: "She was once near and dear to me." Maud: "if I knew who her mother was." Fausset pours tea; Mildred "Fay shall pour out the tea." Maud plays Chopin nocturne for husband. Doctor: Brighton/Eastbourne. Bell sent to Eastbourne; Mildred to follow with Meta and under-butler; Fay NOT allowed. "How many days in a fortnight?" "Fourteen." Mildred returns: Maud not at home (lawn-party at Chertsey). "Fay has gone." "To Brussels." Maud's letter: Fay "dreadfully backward... no manners... finishing-school at Brussels... may not see her again for some years." Epilogue: years pass; Mildred becomes happy mother of "fair young daughter" and wife of idolised husband.

**Ch V Without the Wolf.** Enderby Manor, June Sunday (~15 yrs later). Lola (12) reports village fever. George Greswold (Squire; reads *Athenæum*) and Mildred (his wife; violet eyes, golden hair). Lola's characteristics: precocious, adores father; Latin and Horace with father; "Is life always changing?" Fever victims: Johnny Giles, Mary Martin, Mrs Peter & 2 children, Janet Dawson, Andrew Rogers, Mary Rainbow; little Polly Rainbow (fair; carried milk pitcher). Lola took wine/beef-tea/jelly; Bell forbade cottage entry. George: "like Red Riding Hood, only without the wolf." Greswold is "landlord for pleasure," sanitarian-minded. Manor described (William III red brick, pavilions, oak panelling, Lola's octagon room/study in SW pavilion; Wedgwood, bookshelves). Bell (74, white-haired, nursed Lola's grandmother). Dr Porter (burly, grey, yeoman, "everybody's doctor"). Dairy (Minton tiles, Doulton pans); Mrs Wadman's dairy garden well (old, near manure heap) used for dairy 3 weeks; artesian well clean; Mr Thomas (bailiff) pipes. Mrs Wadman's sister from Salisbury had typhoid. Porter: "You have poisoned a whole village." George: "in plain words... the third [milk] must be wrong." George's dismissal of servants.

**Ch VI "Ah! Pity! The lily is withered."** George in despair ("hand of Fate"). Porter on Polly. Lola slightly feverish; Mildred alarmed. George at Nain-widow image. Mrs Rainbow: "O, sir, she was my all!" "Ah, sir, you'd know it better if it was your young lady." Scotland trip postponed; Dr Hutchinson. Lola delirious; asks about Polly; bell tolls for Polly's funeral; Lola dies ~10 days later; bell tolls. George: "She was the morning... the spring-time." Lola's coffin under white blossoms.

**Ch VII Drifting Apart.** George & Mildred at villa on Lake of Thun (Switzerland) for the rest of the year; St Bernard. George's "bad dream": "The cage—the cage again—iron bars—like a wild beast!" Mildred's backstory: her father sent Fay away; mother Maud's jealousy; Mildred 17 when met George at The Hook (summer, year after Maud's death? — text: mother died after Mildred's 16th birthday; George came ~1 yr later). Mildred remembers Fay's vanishing; Maud's deathbed: Fay = John's natural daughter, "I hated her because she was your father's daughter." Maud: "you must be very stupid... if you meet that odious girl avoid her as you would a pestilence." Mildred: "It was not Fay's fault." John & Mildred: 6 months Leipzig, Paris; The Hook. Mildred rebuffs "unknown woman" fancies. Bell still runs both houses.

**Ch VIII "Such things were."** George Ransome/Greswold's background: Mapledown, Squire Ransome (sporting, hated George's bookishness; Jacob/Esau rant); George left home after rupture over tenants; mother's £300/yr; explored Greece (Schliemann), Constantinople, Corfu, Cyprus, Switzerland, Florence. (Note: first meeting with Mildred at The Hook; Fausset & George's father Oxford friends; Fausset met George on house-boat at Henley.) Enderby mother died; George inherited, took name Greswold. Post-Lola: George dismisses Wadman, Mrs Wadman, bailiff John Thomas (emigrated to Canada), housekeeper; "clean sweep" (Bell delighted). Mildred in Lola's octagon room; plays "La ci darem la mano." Lola's grave: white marble cross, "Laura, the only child of George and Mildred Greswold, aged twelve." Mountain-ash, yew. George at grave: "Judgment! judgment!"

**Ch IX The Face in the Church.** July. Village turns cool to George. Mildred's charity. Rollinson (curate): "Mrs. Greswold is getting over her loss." George: "Such things were." Conversation about George's secrets; "Let us not talk of these things." Plan: invite niece Pamela Ransome (Rosalind now married; Pamela's "fine pair of sisters"). Sunday: Mildred sees stranger in church: auburn hair/beard, reddish-brown eyes, Judas-like mouth. "Whoever he is, I hope I shall never see him again."

**Ch X There Is Always the Skeleton.** Riverdale (Hillersdon wagonette). Louise Hillersdon's history (Louise Lorraine; Great Exhibition '62; German princes, Café de Paris; married Tom Hillersdon; now pious, Evangelical meetings). Luke Thomas (wheelwright, brother of John Thomas). Mrs Rainbow sobs "as I lost my Polly." Castellani calls (groom in Hillersdon livery; "Mr. Castellani"). Castellani gives unsealed letter from Diana Tomkison ("Nepenthe... A vous de cœur"). Castellani's family history (grandfather corresponding clerk at Felix & Sons, Lyons; father's loan; mother convent-educated at Roehampton, knew Fausset). Saw golden child Mildred in Park. Mildred's "I had a daughter." Castellani: Nepenthe a "gift of forgetfulness." Music: Castellani plays Schubert's "Ave Maria," Chopin Etude in C sharp minor. George arrives: Castellani says he met George at Milan assemblies and at Lady Lochinvar's palace at Nice "soon after your first marriage." George pale; Kassandra licks him. Realization: George had been married before.

**Ch XI The Beginning of Doubt.** Clock strikes six. Castellani leaves for Riverdale (Romsey Abbey evensong). Mildred: "why did you not tell me?" George: "My first marriage is a sad remembrance... only an episode." Mildred: "Such things were; but let us not talk of them." Pamela arrives with Box (son of Brockenhurst Joe). Pamela: plump, flaxen, fox-terrier. Pamela on Nepenthe: "I am an Agnostic." Mildred describes Castellani: "red-brown... falsehood." Night reverie: Mildred suspects Mrs-divorce/bigamy issue; fear of "wicked wife"; imagines first love.

**Ch XII "She cannot be unworthy."** Castellani returns Friday; Cancellor (Vicar of St Elizabeth's) is at Riverdale, to preach Hospital Sunday. Castellani: "Mrs. Hillersdon... clever woman." Castellani: Louise Hillersdon may visit with Cancellor; Mildred: "If Mr. Cancellor likes her she cannot be unworthy." Castellani sings Heine/Don Giovanni improvisation; tenor. Castellani offers help with Enderby concert (Burne-Jones window fund, 7 September). Mildred's distrust.

**Ch XIII "Shall she be less than another?"** Cancellor's character (ascetic, Dante/Pascal scholar, slums of Marylebone; Louise Hillersdon's "coadjutor" for 20 yrs). Louise's cunning: wins clergy with gifts. Mildred's tea with Louise, Cancellor, Rollinson, Castellani. Deceased Wife's Sister Bill debate: George argues ("Shall Rachel be withheld..."); Cancellor: "unholy." Rollinson: "a second mother-in-law" jest. George: "The married man who is inconstant..." Mildred asks Castellani to sing; he sings Heine's Ballads. Mildred weeps. Concert invitation; Castellani: "only too glad of an excuse to return to this house." Mildred warns Pamela; Pamela: "How I wish I were César Castellani."

**Ch XIV "Lifting the curtain."** Concert prep: Castellani organizes; Pamela duets ("'Twere sweet to die as the roses die"); Lady Millborough; Miss Tadcasters. Castellani improvises "St Partridge Day." Castellani: "There is always a skeleton." He hints Vivien died "infinitely sad." Mildred resolves to question George. Dinner; study; George shows morocco-case cabinet photograph of first wife (small delicate face, large dark eyes, "a nature wanting the element of repose"). Mildred faints. **END VOL I.**

---

## VOLUME II — Book the Second: LACHESIS; or the Meter of Destiny

**Ch I A Wife and No Wife.** Castellani's social mystery (Magnus Dudley: "natural son of Cavour's"? rumours; Whitechapel ice-seller). *Nepenthe* success. Castellani at Riverdale ("Wandering Jew" banter with Louise). He calls Pamela "genus girl" detestable; Louise: Pamela ~£1500/yr. Castellani on George: "troubles... not a gossip." Concert day (7 Sept): Pamela & Castellani sing "Flow on, thou shining river"; Pamela fantasises Madame Castellani. Mildred ill. George at Salisbury. Mildred's plan: sleeps none; letters to George & Pamela; leaves in carriage to Ivy Cottage (Miss Fisher, Romsey) then Romsey Station; George finds her gone. Mildred's letter to George: "that photograph is a portrait of my unhappy sister"; "our marriage was against the law of God and man"; "life-long separation"; "Do not follow me."

**Ch II The Sins of the Fathers.** George reads letter; Vivien Faux (met Florence ~19 yrs before; Mortimers; married under name Vivien Faux before British Consul at Florence; she had £30,000 at 21 via lawyer in Lincoln's Inn). Bell interview: "she was the image of him"; "Miss Fay... natural daughter"; Bell hints Gertrude had no child; Bell's "who first mooted"—Bell was the source. Bell says Fay watched beside Mildred's bed; "she was like Miss Lola." George: "My God, this is fatality!"

**Ch III The Verdict of Her Church.** Mildred at Waterloo; Mrs Tomkison (Cecilia; literary; Adam = "Mexican Street Railways"). Castellani's rooms in Queen Anne's Mansions ("Materialisation"). George's cold letter: defends marriage with deceased wife's sister; disputes identity; "bigot"; proposes Fay's paternity unproven. Mildred's reply: her mother's death-bed evidence; Cancellor taught her faith. Mildred sees Cancellor; tells all; Cancellor: "legally you may still be George Greswold's wife... incestuous marriage." Mildred: "Not one word more... The bond is broken." Cancellor: "self-sacrifice is the shortest road to happiness." Mildred: going to aunt in Brighton.

**Ch IV No Light.** Gertrude Fausset (57) in Lewes Crescent; silver-gray drawing-rooms; French Directory furniture; Broadwood piano; St Edmund's (Gothic, near). Brighton gossip about her wealth. Mildred confides; Gertrude: mother was "bundle of nerves," "forget... go back to your duty." Gertrude: "I was a foreigner... went to Milan with a chaperon"; "Gertrude's vow never to marry." Gertrude: Fay "died abroad... two or three years" before marriage; "I never heard your husband was a widower." Mildred's clothing: black lace gown; locket "L.G." Castellani at piano (Bach fugue). Castellani's account: knows aunt "fifteen years"; "Miss Fausset was all goodness to me when I was an idle undergraduate." Castellani dines; "Paolo Castellani" music (Mildred recognises "La Donna del Pittore" duet). Gertrude: "We are not a musical nation"; Gertrude's Milan years. Castellani kisses Gertrude's hand.

**Ch V The Future Might Be Darker.** George's grief; he visits Pergament & Pergament (Lincoln's Inn Fields). Clerk; Mr Pergament (bald, ~45, oak office). Pergament knows "Ransome"; asks about "sad circumstances" (wife's death). Refuses to identify Fay's father; "oath." Penknife jerk at "Fausset." George suspects Fausset's paternity. Pamela & Box at Hanover Square hotel. George visits Mrs Tomkison (Queen Anne's Gate). George & Pamela: "Mr. Castellani ... indirectly... began the mischief." Pamela suspects jealousy. Brighton: hotel on East Cliff. George & Mildred's parting in Lewes Crescent drawing-room: "Mildred, is it irrevocable?" "Cancellor... fanatic." George: "Good-bye... The future might be still darker for us if we did not so part." Pamela stays with Gertrude. Maltravers (Vicar of St Edmund's) and Rev. Percival Cromer call. Maltravers: confessional knowledge of Gertrude; "veil lifted."

**Ch VI Higher Views.** Mildred's "low fever"; doctor. Castellani visits Lewes Crescent; hotel on cliff. Pamela & Castellani sing; Box trained. Mildred: "I am afraid... you are beginning to think too much about him." Mildred resolves to leave for Pallanza (Lago Maggiore); courier Albrecht. Castellani "infinitely higher." Gertrude: Castellani "belongs to the butterfly species"; "Let her marry the man she loves." Maltravers wants Mildred to build transept. Mildred's aversion: Castellani's touch. Castellani to Gertrude: "I have other views... Infinitely higher."

**Ch VII The Time Has Come.** Left Brighton for Italy (with Pamela, Albrecht, Louisa). Pallanza: winter; Castellani follows; appears on hills at sundown, with Pamela; music ("I waited for the Lord"; Heine songs). Castellani's "magnetic power." Mildred's ultimatum (Feb.): "The time has come... From to-day your visits must cease." Castellani's declaration; Mildred: "They will hold me to my dying hour." Castellani: "Yes, to a madman and a murderer."

**Ch VIII Not Proven.** Castellani's accusation: George Ransome "shrewdly suspected of having made away with his wife," confined at asylum near Nice (St André). Mildred to Nice; Albrecht. Pamela's distress. Hôtel Westminster, Promenade des Anglais. Mildred visits Lady Lochinvar (Palais Montano, Nice; Lady L was Lady Castle-Connell's school friend; husband Lord Lochinvar). Lady L: Ransome couple seen at Nice 17 years ago; wife Vivien died falling from cliff at St Jean (Villefranche) path; husband arrested, later asylum. Lady L: "It is a case of not proven." Mildred reveals identity to Lady L.

**Ch IX Looking Back.** Lady L's advice; Mildred to St Jean; Le Bout du Monde (now Montfleuri); market-woman; cliff path; "Madame, the cook was my cousin." Mildred revisits Vivien's garden (berceau, fountain). Pamela attends Lady L's opera with Mr Stuart. Drive to St André asylum: madman singer (Spanish nobleman); Dr Leroy; Maria Castellani (ex-prima donna, Paolo's cousin, "Lucrezia Borgia"; asylum); Paolo "made her his creature... married a Frenchwoman"; Mildred identifies Paolo's music; Mildred visits George Ransome's old room. Ends Vol II.

---

## VOLUME III — Book the Third: ATROPOS; or That Which Must Be

**Ch I A Wrecked Life.** Dr Leroy's garden tour; Maria Castellani sings Lucrezia; "I owed him nothing." Maria's story: Paolo deserted her; married a French consumptive heiress; her ruin. Mildred offers to fund a piano/room (declined). Pamela & Stuart; Lady Lochinvar's invitation. Mildred to have tea with Stuart at Westminster.

**Ch II In the Morning of Life.** George at Enderby, alone; reads Pamela's letters (Mildred at Lady L's). George's backstory: father Squire Ransome (Mapledown; "nutmeg-grater" remark; Rebecca/Jacob), brother Randolph; George's travels (Greece, Schliemann, Constantinople); Florence winter; meets Vivien Faux at Signora Vicenti's party (Beethoven symphony); she: "The man I thought the noblest... did me the greatest wrong." Mortimer chaperone (dreary artist). Picnic (American lady); Vivien's tears; "I love you." Marriage within a month (March). Vivien refuses England ("people would want to know who I am"). Lived Oberland, Engadine, then Nice; Lady Lochinvar; Vivien's jealousy; hysterics; villa at St Jean (March).

**Ch III The Rift in the Lute.** St Jean villa (orange groves, peach cluster, Dijon roses, Villefranche view, Eza, Turbia). Vivien's jealousy: "pity." Boat conversation. Meeting on the common above St Jean with Delia Darcy & sister (white gowns, Leghorn hats; carriage). Vivien scatters rosemary; quarrel: "Say that you wish me dead." Path on cliff opposite Beaulieu. George: "I have sometimes thought of death." Silence; rush of skirts. Vivien over cliff, lying in rocks; boat picks her up (fishermen); dead.

**Ch IV Darkness.** Juge d'Instruction, Villefranche; George arrested; lock-up overnight; Byron "She died, but not alone." Bell tolls; burial at dawn. George's madness (political offender; "President of Italian Republic"). Asylum at St André ("great white house", iron-barred colonnade). Wakes; "August 22." George returns to villa; visits grave on hill. Summoned to England early next year for mother's death. Vivien's stone: "VIVIEN RANSOME. Died April 24th, 1868. Eternally lamented."

**Ch V The Grave on the Hill.** Mildred at Nice; Lady L likes Pamela; Pamela & Malcolm Stuart (plain, honest; freckled; "Sir Henry" comparison; reads Darwin/Quarterlies; Pamela cool to Castellani). Mildred's visits to St Jean; villagers call her "English Madonna." Mildred plants rose-cross (Gloire de Dijon, Maréchal Niel) on Vivien's grave on hill above Villefranche.

**Ch VI Pamela Changes Her Mind.** Castellani follows to Nice (Cosmopolitan Hotel); Albrecht gossip; Mrs Montagu W. Brown (American); Pamela's flower battle; Castellani on carriage (coat, pale buff, gardenia); Pamela cold; comparison with Stuart. Lady L invites Pamela to Palais Montano. Maltravers' letter re Gertrude's failing health. Pamela: "I am beginning to adore Nice." Pamela promises to drop Castellani.

**Ch VII As the Sands Run Down.** Mildred returns to Brighton (Lewes Crescent). Gertrude failing; "I am a doomed woman." Gertrude asks about Fay's death; Mildred tells her Fay's suicide; Gertrude hides knowledge. Gertrude asks about father's papers. Gertrude: John died in Parchment Street of pneumonia (autumn, London fog). Gertrude: "I was not sent for." Gertrude: "My brother loved me for my own sake." Gertrude's tea-callers; Maltravers (pleaded for Brighton); "flash of the falchion." Mildred's letters (to Rollinson; reply: "his heart is broken"; George visits daughter's grave at dusk). Mildred decides to see George. Enderby churchyard at dusk: George at Lola's grave; Mildred: "George! George!"

**Ch VIII "How should I greet thee?"** George cold: "What brings you here, Mildred?" "My heart is buried here." Mildred kisses marble. George: "I was to blame... lost control." Mildred: "Your dreams have told me." George: "Good-night and good-bye." Mildred to Rollinson's lodgings (Mrs Mason). Tea-dinner (pig's trotters). Rollinson: "You have broken his heart." Salisbury inn night. Brighton; Gertrude's dull house; Mildred plans Italian Lakes/Cornwall; Gertrude refuses. Gertrude's Milan years revealed as vague. Pamela engaged to Stuart; wedding in Westminster Abbey; The Hook as honeymoon. Mildred's visit to The Hook (housekeeper Mrs Dawson; father's study untouched).

**Ch IX Litera Scripta Manet.** The Hook: Mildred revisits; father's study. Cupboard search: pigeon-holes; bundle of ~20 letters tied with red ribbon, indorsed "M. F."; by Gertrude (to brother John). Letters: Milan Conservatoire (Mrs Holmby chaperon; Cathedral vespers; Castellani's opera at La Scala; Castellani introduced by 'cellist). Gertrude's fall: Evian (Lake Geneva) letters: pregnancy; child "dishonour"; plan to hand infant to nurse at Dijon; "I shall never look upon its face again." Later letters: child placed with old lady at Barnes; named Fanny → Fay; Gertrude's fury; "get the girl out of your house"; settlement £30,000 India Stock to "Fanny Fausset, otherwise Vivien Faux," on 21st birthday. Mildred: "Fool, fool, fool!" Mildred writes to Gertrude: never enter her house again; going back to George. Catches train Chertsey–Reading.

**Ch X Marked by Fate.** Mildred arrives Enderby ~10 p.m.; library; George; "Have we not parted often enough?" Mildred kneels, confesses; George kisses her. "Whose child was she?" Mildred: "Fay was my blood-relation... not my sister." George: "One cannot make a broken vase new again." Village gossip (Mrs Porter, doctor's wife). Mildred's heart weak; Porter calls Jenner/Clark. George in despair ("marked out by Fate"). Shrubbery walk. London consultation in Cavendish Square: heart disease like Maud's mother; "cherish her as a hothouse flower."

**Ch XI Like a Tale That Is Told.** Pamela's wedding in Westminster Abbey (Smithson gown; society papers). Honeymoon at The Hook (punt). Gertrude's summons (Aug.); Mildred & George at Brighton hotel (East Cliff). Gertrude's confession: loved Paolo Castellani; civil marriage in Milan a sham (dingy office; Milanese attorney); fled to Vevay; learned he was married; child born Evian; gave Fay to Barnes; Castellani's son César knew all and "pretended to be fond of me." Mildred: "Let the past be forgotten... let us part in love." Gertrude dies early winter (first frost). Mildred inherits; Greswold Hospital founded in south London; George dies after; line ended. Castellani, enriched by Gertrude's legacy, remains in silly circles; *Nepenthe* reputation fades.

**THE END.**
